title: Completion comparison and congruence extension through an elementary etale chart
statement: Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth], let $X,Y$ be schemes locally of finite type over $S$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $x\in X$, $y\in Y$ lie over the same point of $S$. Let $p:U\to X$ be an etale morphism [def-weil-etale-morphism] of $S$-schemes, let $u\in U$ with $p(u)=x$, and suppose $p$ induces an isomorphism $\kappa(x)\to\kappa(u)$ [def-weil-residue-field]. Let $f:U\to Y$ be an $S$-morphism with $f(u)=y$. Put $A=\mathcal O_{Y,y}$, $B=\mathcal O_{X,x}$, $C=\mathcal O_{U,u}$, with maximal ideals $\mathfrak m_A,\mathfrak m_B,\mathfrak m_C$, and let $\widehat A,\widehat B,D=\widehat C$ be their maximal-ideal-adic completions, with canonical maps $\iota_A,\iota_B,\iota_C$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Denote by $\widehat p^{\sharp}:\widehat B\to D$ and $g=\widehat f^{\sharp}:\widehat A\to D$ the maps induced by the actual stalk maps on all maximal-ideal-power quotients. Fix an isomorphism of rings $\varphi:\widehat A\xrightarrow{\sim}\widehat B$ and an integer $N\geq1$. Suppose $g(\iota_A(a))-\widehat p^{\sharp}(\varphi(\iota_A(a)))\in\mathfrak m_C^ND$ for every $a\in A$. Then $Y$ is locally Noetherian and $A,B,C$ are Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]; $D$ is local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak m_CD$; $\widehat p^{\sharp}$ is an isomorphism, so $\alpha=\widehat p^{\sharp}\circ\varphi:\widehat A\xrightarrow{\sim}D$ is an isomorphism; and the actual completed map $g$ satisfies $g(z)-\alpha(z)\in\mathfrak n^N$ for every $z\in\widehat A$.

source.place: Tag 0CAV, lemma-isomorphism-approximation, proof: comparison of the X and U completions by lemma-flat-unramified, and the congruence diagram before passage to associated graded rings; the congruence is extended from the original local ring.

proof.text: Apply [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft] to $X\to S$ and $Y\to S$: both $X$ and $Y$ are locally Noetherian. By [def-weil-etale-morphism], $p$ is locally of finite presentation; a finite presentation is in particular a finite set of algebra generators, so [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] and [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] imply that $p$ is locally of finite type. Apply [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft] again, now over $X$, to obtain that $U$ is locally Noetherian. For each of $x,y,u$, choose a Noetherian affine chart in the covering of [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Its stalk is the localization of its coordinate ring at the point, by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-map-stalk-localization]. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian] makes $A,B,C$ Noetherian. Their maximal ideals are finitely generated by [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring].

source.place: Tag 01T6, lemma-finite-type-noetherian; Tag 00FN, lemma-Noetherian-permanence; affine stalk identification Tag 01HV

proof.text: The actual stalk map $p_u^\sharp:B\to C$ is local and flat: locality is part of [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism], and flatness follows by unpacking [def-weil-etale-morphism] and [def-weil-flat-morphism]. Choose affine etale charts $\operatorname{Spec}T\subset U$ and $\operatorname{Spec}R\subset X$ around $u,x$ with $p(\operatorname{Spec}T)\subset\operatorname{Spec}R$, as in [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Write $Q\subset T$ and $P\subset R$ for the corresponding primes. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-map-stalk-localization], the stalk map is $R_P\to T_Q$ and $B=R_P$, $C=T_Q$. The statement [lem-weil-pbc-etale-prime-generates-maximal] gives $PT_Q=QT_Q=\mathfrak m_C$. Since the ideal generated by $P$ in $R_P$ is $\mathfrak m_B$, extending it to $T_Q$ gives exactly $PT_Q$; hence $\mathfrak m_BC=\mathfrak m_C$. The residue-field map of this very local homomorphism is an isomorphism by the hypothesis on $p$.

source.place: Tag 00U4, lemma-etale-at-prime (1), supplying the maximal-ideal hypothesis of Tag 0AGX

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-completion-iso] to $B\to C$, with Noetherianness from step 1 and the flatness, maximal-ideal equality, and residue isomorphism from step 2. Its coordinatewise completed map is exactly $\widehat p^\sharp$ as specified in the statement, so $\widehat p^\sharp$ is an isomorphism. Consequently $\alpha=\widehat p^\sharp\circ\varphi$ is an isomorphism. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-local-ring] to $A$ and $C$. This gives that $D$ is local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak m_CD$, and that $\widehat A$ is local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak a=\mathfrak m_A\widehat A$. A ring isomorphism preserves units in both directions, and hence sends the unique maximal ideal (the nonunits) onto the unique maximal ideal. Therefore $\alpha(\mathfrak a)=\mathfrak n$ and $\alpha(\mathfrak a^N)=\mathfrak n^N$.

source.place: Tag 0AGX, lemma-flat-unramified; Tags 05GG, lemma-hathat-finitely-generated, and 05GI, lemma-radical-completion

proof.text: Fix any $z\in\widehat A$. The maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_A$ is finitely generated by step 1, so [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-power] applies to $(A,\mathfrak m_A,N)$. Choose $a\in A$ representing the $N$-th coordinate of $z$ in $A/\mathfrak m_A^N$. Since the projection composed with $\iota_A$ is the quotient map and its kernel is $\mathfrak m_A^N\widehat A$, we obtain $e=z-\iota_A(a)\in\mathfrak m_A^N\widehat A=\mathfrak a^N$. Here $(\mathfrak m_A\widehat A)^N=\mathfrak m_A^N\widehat A$ follows by expanding products of ideal generators in each direction.

source.place: Tag 05GG, lemma-hathat-finitely-generated, applied to the ring as a module over itself

proof.text:
The stalk map $f_u^\sharp:A\to C$ is local by [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism]. The definition of $g$ on quotient coordinates gives $g\iota_A=\iota_C f_u^\sharp$. Thus $g\iota_A(\mathfrak m_A)\subseteq\mathfrak m_CD=\mathfrak n$. Every element of $\mathfrak a$ is a finite sum of products $\iota_A(b)d$ with $b\in\mathfrak m_A$ and $d\in\widehat A$; applying $g$ shows $g(\mathfrak a)\subseteq\mathfrak n$, and expanding products gives $g(\mathfrak a^N)\subseteq\mathfrak n^N$. For the $a,e$ of step 4, both $g(e)$ and $\alpha(e)$ belong to $\mathfrak n^N$, by this inclusion and step 3. Finally
$$g(z)-\alpha(z)=[g(\iota_A(a))-\alpha(\iota_A(a))]+g(e)-\alpha(e).$$
The bracket lies in $\mathfrak m_C^ND=(\mathfrak m_CD)^N=\mathfrak n^N$ by the assumed congruence on $A$. All three summands lie in that ideal, proving the required congruence for every $z$.
